column1: ## Please refer to the manual for more details
# Parameters can be prefixed by a distribution specifier
# (f fixed, u uniform, n normal, l lognormal, e exponential, g geometric)
## When using the G mode, these events use genome-wise rate.
## The next three events can have gene-family rates when using the Gm mode.
## Rates represent the frequency (and fixation probability) of the different
## events measure in time units (see your Species Tree)
## The next three events use always genome-wise rates
## Extensions. Extensions determine how many contiguous genes are affected by a
## REPLACEMENT_TRANSFER gives the probability of the transfer being a
## replacement transfer. REPLACEMENT_TRANSFER = 0 if all transfers are additive
# If ASSORTATIVE_TRANSFER is True, the transfer occur preferentially between
# closely related lineages. The weighted probability is proportional to e ^ -
#   Can be computationally expensive, use at your discretion
## MIN_GENOME_SIZE prevents genome to become too small. Any losses affecting
## genomes under this size will be ignored
## Output related parameters. Use SCALE_TREE != 0 only if you used that too in
## the Species Tree mode. Use the same number
# Include the whole path to the parameters file. The parameters file has a first
# line (header) and 4 tab separated columns with the name of the gene family
# If SCALE_RATES is True, it will scale the rates used in the parameters file to
# the height of the tree, from the leaves to the root node (not the initial
# node, remember that Zombi also simulates the stem above the root). Value
## SEED : If 0, the SEED is chosen randomly
